Thank you for bringing the WordPress Credits Program to your institution. This guide covers the Institution Dashboard, the page your institution has on the Education Directory: your students and the lists you can download, enrolling more of them, the semester report, your institution's details and how to correct them, your colleagues, and your Collaboration Agreement.

It is written for the people who act for an institution. The program's Administrators have a guide of their own.

Signing in

Nobody registers on this site, and there is no sign-up form: the program makes every account for the person it belongs to. That means two things on your first visit:

  1. Go to the site's login page and use Lost your password? with the email address on your account. A reset link arrives at that address.
  2. Set a password, and you are in - unless your account also asks for a code, which the next part covers.

If the reset email never arrives, the address on your account is probably not the one you are checking. The login page cannot change it - ask whoever runs the program.

Signing in with a code

Besides your password, your account may ask for a code. Whether it does is the program's choice, and it is made for every account of your kind at once. When it does, there is nothing to set up first: from your next sign-in, the code arrives by email. When it does not, signing in works as described above, and a card on your page invites you to turn the code on for yourself.

After you enter your username and password, a second screen asks for the code. Which kind depends on how your account is set up.

An emailed code. The screen says a verification code has been sent to the email address on your account. The email comes from this site and has Login confirmation code in its subject line. It holds a code of eight digits. Type it into Verification Code and press Verify. A code works once, and for fifteen minutes. Resend Code sends a new one and the new one replaces the old, so use the newest email.

An authenticator app. If you have set one up, the screen asks for the code from your app instead: Authentication Code. Open the app, find this site in it, and type the six digits it shows. The digits change every 30 seconds, so type the ones on the screen at that moment.

A wrong code does not lock you out for good, but the site makes you wait a moment before the next try, and the wait grows with every wrong code, up to fifteen minutes. Wait it out, then type the code again, carefully.

Setting up an authenticator app

An app on your phone is quicker than waiting for an email, and it keeps working when your inbox does not. The card at the top of your page starts it. Its heading is Add a second step to your sign-in when the code is yours to choose, and Your account asks for a code when you sign in when the program asks for one; its button, Turn on two-factor authentication or Set up an authenticator app, opens your profile screen at its Two-Factor Options. Ignoring the card costs nothing: signing in keeps working the way it does now.

If you already use emailed codes and you open that screen more than about ten minutes after you signed in, it first asks you to confirm with Revalidate now, which takes one more code. Then follow the steps on the screen: install an authenticator app on your phone (any will do, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator), scan the QR code the screen shows with it, and type in the code your app then displays. Once the app is set up the card stops appearing.

Before you leave that screen, generate the recovery codes (the card calls them backup codes) and keep them somewhere other than your phone. Each works once, and the screen shows them only once. They are how you get back in if you lose the phone.

If you cannot get your code

  • The email does not come. Look in your spam folder, then press Resend Code. The email goes to the address on your account, so if you no longer read that mailbox, an emailed code cannot reach you.
  • Your phone or your app is gone. Under Having Problems? on the same screen, the site lists any other way your account has, for example Send a code to your email, or Use a recovery code if you saved some. Type one of your saved recovery codes where the screen asks for it, and cross that code off, because it will not work twice.
  • You have neither. Without the emailed code, the app or a recovery code, the site cannot tell that it is you, and it lets nobody past that screen. Tell whoever runs the program that you are locked out, and give them the username you sign in with. This guide cannot fix it for you.

Once you are signed in

Your page is drawn for whoever is signed in, so the same address shows each person their own page, and no change to a link shows anybody else's. The program's Administrators are the one exception: to help, they can open anyone's page, through a switcher only they are shown. A company's people share one Sponsor Dashboard, and an institution's people share one Institution Dashboard, though a tutor sees less of it.

Your Institution Dashboard

Your institution's page on the Education Directory is the Institution Dashboard, at /institution-dashboard/. You reach it after signing in with the account the program made for you, or the one made for you when you accepted a colleague's invitation; everybody the program attached to your institution shares this one page, though a tutor sees less of it. A card above the page may invite you to set up a code for signing in, or tell you the program asks for one: Signing in, at the start of this guide, covers it.

What you read about your students comes from the program's records, which this site reads at intervals and not each time you open the page. A line says when: "Read from the program records on" a date, and how long ago that was. It sits under the figures on the Overview and at the foot of the roster on Students. A change an Administrator makes in the program's records can take a while to reach the page.

The menu

The page is drawn in a frame. A bar across the top holds the site's name, Homepage, and your photo and first name, with Log out behind them. A menu runs down the side, and the view you are reading sits beside it. Each item in the menu is a view of its own, at its own address, in this order:

  • Overview, where the page opens.
  • Students: your roster, and a student's card.
  • Enroll students, once the program has switched enrollment on for institutions.
  • Semester reports: the reports the program prepares for your institution.
  • Your institution: the cards Your institution's details and Representatives and tutors. A tutor sees Representatives and tutors alone.
  • Agreement: your Collaboration Agreement.
  • Events, while there is an event from the program's sponsors, or from the program, to join.
  • Program updates, while the program has published an update for institutions. It opens the newest in the same frame, with the other updates listed beside it when there are more.

A tutor's menu has no Enroll students and no Events. Until your Collaboration Agreement is accepted, a representative's menu holds only Overview and Agreement, and Program updates when there is one. A tutor cannot open the page until then. Before your agreement is accepted, below, says what a representative does.

Under Help come:

  • the Ask box, "Ask about the program", whenever the program has switched its question assistant on for institutions. It answers questions about the program and about WordPress from the WordPress documentation, and links back to the pages its answers came from. Your question is sent to an outside AI service, so do not type anything confidential.
  • Institution guide, which opens this guide.
  • #wpcredits on Slack, which opens the WordPress Credits Slack channel.
  • Write to the program, which opens a mail to the Administrator your institution is assigned to, once the program has assigned one and has an address for them.

Beside a view's name, a red tag counts what waits for you in it, for example "1 waits". Beside Overview, the tag counts everything that waits. Waiting for you, below, says what is counted.

Each view but the Overview opens with its name and one sentence that says what it holds. Agreement opens under the name Collaboration Agreement. A view has no link back of its own: the menu is the way back. Students leads from a student's card back to the roster, with the filters you had set, and Semester reports leads from a report back to the list.

A view whose cards have nothing to show says "Nothing to show here yet." When you press a button, what happened is said on the same view: a form that could not be sent says why above that form, a button on a row of a list says what happened above the list's rows, and anything else is said at the top of its card.

On a narrower screen the menu shows its icons alone, and on a phone it opens as a drawer from the Menu button at the top and closes with Close menu. On a wide screen, Collapse menu at its foot folds it to its icons, and your browser remembers that.

The Overview

The Overview opens with your institution's name, with the icon of your institution's own website beside it when that website has one. Under the name are the city and country, the website as a link, and "Contact:" with the name of the person the program writes to. They are what the program has on record for your institution. A representative corrects them on the card Your institution's details, on Your institution: Your details, your representatives and your agreement covers it. Enroll students, beside them, opens the Enroll students view while it is in your menu.

Next comes a row of figures for the semester the Students view opens on: how many students signed up, how many graduated, how many are waiting to graduate, how many are on the program now and how many are waiting for a mentor. Since 1.123.98 a student waiting to graduate has a figure of their own, and "on the program now" and "waiting for a mentor" no longer count them, so the figures after "signed up" never add up to more than it. A figure with nothing to count is left out, and with nothing at all to count there is no row of figures and no line under it.

Waiting for you

Waiting for you has one row for each thing that waits for you to act. Each row has a red "Waits" tag, says what waits, gives one sentence about it, and ends with a button that opens the view and the card that hold it:

  • Collaboration Agreement not signed yet, Collaboration Agreement returned or Collaboration Agreement revoked, with Open the agreement, while your agreement waits for your institution. A signed copy you uploaded waits for an Administrator, not for you, so it is no row.
  • A checked list of students waits to be created, with Open the list, while a list you checked on Enroll students has not been created. When nothing waits, the Overview says "Nothing waits for you." The tag says "Waits" in words, so the red is never the only sign.

Good to know

Good to know follows when there is something to say that waits for nobody. Its rows are counted nowhere.

  • A list of students is being created, tagged "In progress", while the list is being created. It carries on by itself.
  • Your semester report for a semester is ready, with "Approved on" and the day, and Read the report, for thirty days after an Administrator approves it.
  • Your request was decided, with what became of your request to correct your institution's name and address, and See your details, for thirty days after it was decided and until the next request is sent. A row tagged "New" is news. It waits for nothing, and nothing has to be done about it.

Since 1.123.98 four facts about your students follow, each with no tag and See them, which lists the students it counts. They are counted nowhere, and each is there only while it counts at least one student. They count your students of every semester, where the figures above count the one semester named under them, so a fact and a figure with the same words can differ:

  • 2 students have not signed in yet: students on the program now or waiting for a mentor, whose account here was made since the site began recording sign-ins (the day a student's card names) and who have no sign-in on record. Accounts made before that day are not counted, because the site kept no sign-in record before then. "Open a student to send them an invitation." The page says only whether a sign-in is on record, never when. A tutor is not shown it.
  • 2 students finish within 30 days: students on the program now or waiting for a mentor whose end date is today or in the next 30 days.
  • 1 placement ended and is still open: students on the program now or waiting for a mentor whose end date has passed. "The end date has passed and the student is still on the program. Correct the date if the placement goes on." On the student's card, correct the date under Correct this student's details, or record how the placement ended under Finishing this placement. A graduation the card does not offer, or a student with no account, goes through your contact at the program. A tutor is not shown it.
  • 1 student is waiting to graduate: "The program is checking their work." and, when the site knows it, the day the wait began. There is nothing for you to do.

What your students work on

What your students work on (since 1.123.98) follows when there is something to say: a table of the teams the students of the semester the Students view opens on contribute to, with how many students are on each, most first, counted as the semester report counts its Contribution Teams; then one line that says how many different mentors your students on the program now have and, of that semester's students, for how many hours are on record. A student on two teams counts for each, and a student counts for hours when more than zero hours are on record. The page does not say why a student has no hours on record. The teams are counted from today's roster; a semester report keeps the numbers of the day it was made and takes each student's team from its own records, so the two can differ.

Your contact at the program

Your contact at the program ends the Overview: the Administrator your institution is assigned to, with a link to write to them when the program has an address for them, and Book a call when it has a booking link. It is there once an Administrator is assigned to your institution. It says "They look after your institution. Write to them about anything the guide does not answer."

Before your agreement is accepted

Until an Administrator has accepted a signed Collaboration Agreement for your institution, or recorded one the program already holds, a representative's menu holds Overview and Agreement, and any other address of the page opens the Overview. A tutor is shown no page until then. The Overview has your institution's name and your contact at the program. While the agreement waits for your institution, Waiting for you has a row with Open the agreement. While a signed copy waits for review, or the program's records do not agree yet, it says "Nothing waits for you." Agreement opens under the name Collaboration Agreement, and what it says depends on where your agreement stands.

No agreement recorded yet

With no agreement recorded, Agreement says "The program has no Collaboration Agreement recorded for your institution. Until it does, its representatives reach only the Overview and the Agreement, and its tutors no page." Then it gives three steps.

  1. Get the agreement. Generate the agreement makes the program's own template with the name you type in The institution's name ("Exactly as it should print on the agreement."). When the template exists in more than one language, choose one in Language. The document opens as a page your browser can save as a PDF or print. Nothing is sent to the program yet. You may use an agreement of your own instead; an Administrator reads it in full, so it takes longer.
  2. Have it signed by somebody who can commit your institution.
  3. Upload the signed PDF. Choose "The program's template, signed" or "An agreement of our own, signed". Tick the box that says it is signed by somebody who can commit the institution. Pick the file with Choose a file and press Upload the signed agreement. The file must be a PDF without a password.

Under the steps the page says that an institution that already signed an agreement with the program need not sign again: an Administrator can record the copy the program holds, and your account opens when they do. If that is you, write to your contact at the program.

The other states

  • Generated. The page says on what day you generated the program's agreement and which template version it was, and that it is not signed and uploaded yet. Open that document again, in the first step, gives you the same document, with the name it was made with, and the three steps and the sentence about an agreement already signed stay as they were.
  • Waiting for review. Tagged Waiting for review, the page says "We received your signed agreement on" a date, and that an Administrator will review it and you will get an email either way. Download the copy we hold gives you the file back, and Withdraw it deletes the file from this site so that you can upload another.
  • Returned. Tagged Returned, the page says "An Administrator returned your agreement, with this note:" and shows the note, with who left it and on which day, and a form to upload the corrected agreement, signed, as a PDF.
  • Revoked. Tagged Revoked, the page says the program revoked the agreement, and that until a new agreement is accepted its representatives reach only the Overview and the Agreement, and its tutors no page. It shows the note the program left, with a form to upload a new signed agreement. An Administrator reviews it the same way as the first one.
  • Accepted, but not yet agreed everywhere. If this site holds an accepted agreement and the program's own record does not agree with it yet, the page says an Administrator can see the difference and settles it. There is nothing for you to do.

When an Administrator accepts the agreement, everybody at your institution is emailed, a representative's whole menu opens, and a tutor can open the page. Agreement then shows the accepted agreement: Your Collaboration Agreement covers it.

Events from our sponsors

Events lists the events the program's sponsors host for its students, mentors, Administrators and institutions, when there are any to join. It is in a representative's menu, and not in a tutor's. The list follows the view's name and its sentence, with no heading of its own. Each event shows its host, its day and time in your own time zone, how long it runs and how many places are left, with Join. Once you are on an event the page says "You are on it.", and shows Leave, which gives your place back, and Join the call when the event has a call link. The email you get when you join carries the call link and a calendar file.

Your students

Students, in the menu, is your roster: the students your institution has on the program, by semester and by where they are, with a list a representative can download and a card for each student. It is in your menu once your Collaboration Agreement is accepted. Enrolling more students is a view of its own, Enroll students, described below.

Reading the roster

At the top of the roster one form sets what you see. Cohort is the semester the students started in, each with how many signed up; the roster opens on this semester when you have students in it and on your newest one when you do not. Group is All students or one of the four groups below. Search reads a student's name, WordPress.org username, tutor and field of study; it does not search email addresses. Show applies them, and Clear the filters takes the group and the search off. The address of a filtered page can be sent to a colleague, who lands on the same list.

Under the form, headed with the semester's name, is a summary of the cohort: how many students signed up and how many have graduated, and how that compares with the semester before ("Compared with" the earlier semester and its two numbers, or "No students started in" it).

The students are filed in four groups. Each group is a card of its own, with its count in words beside its name, such as "2 students", and a line under it that says what it holds. A group folds and unfolds with one press on its title; Current and Waiting for a mentor start open, unless a group holds more than twelve students, and Finished and Not on the program now start closed.

  • Current: "With a mentor assigned or a progress record already started, students waiting to graduate included." Since 1.123.98 the Overview's figure "on the program now" leaves out the students waiting to graduate, who have a figure of their own, so this group can hold more students than that figure.
  • Waiting for a mentor: "Signed up, with no mentor assigned and no progress record yet." That is the whole of what the group says. It lists the students the program's records show as signed up with neither, and the page says no more than that.
  • Finished: "Mentoring has finished. Their details are kept for reference."
  • Not on the program now: "Students who have not started yet, never began the program, or stopped before finishing it."

A fifth list, Enrollment not recorded yet, appears only when students are reporting their progress and the program's records hold no enrollment for them. They are not counted in the groups, and the list says an Administrator needs to complete the record.

Each student is a row that opens. The closed row shows the student's photo, or the first letter of their name, the name, the program they are on as a tag, their dates and the name of their mentor when the page has one. A group that holds one student shows that row open. For a student who has an account on this site the name is a link that opens the student's own card, described below. For a student who has none the name is not a link and there is no card of their own; their row in the roster still opens like any other. Opened, a row lists Program, Dates, Days left, Mentor, WordPress.org, Team, Website, Field of study, Tutor and Hours. A row with nothing in it reads "Not recorded". The Mentor row reads "No mentor yet." for a student with none on record. When the program's records name a mentor and the name has not reached the page, the row says so in a sentence of its own instead.

A narrowed list from the Overview

See them, on a row of the Overview, opens Students with that row's students alone (since 1.123.98): one sentence that says what the list is, such as "2 students have not signed in yet.", then Show all students, which brings the whole roster back, then one list with a row per student: the name, a link to the student's card when the student has an account here, the program they are on as a tag, the semester they started in and their dates. There is no form, no group and no semester to choose. The list of students who have not signed in yet adds one line under its sentence: "Accounts made before" the day the site began recording sign-ins "are not counted: the site kept no sign-in record before then." When the list is empty, or the address names a list the Overview does not offer you, Students shows the whole roster. A student's card opened from the list is the ordinary card: Students in the menu leads to the whole roster, and your browser's Back returns to the list.

Opening a student's card

Press a student's name, where it is a link: only a student who has an account on this site has a card. The card opens in place of the roster, under the name Students, and Students in the menu leads back to the roster with the filters you had set. The card shows:

  • the student's name and program, with their photo when they have a WordPress.org profile picture;
  • whether they have signed in yet: for a student who has not, a line says "No sign-in on record since" the day the site began recording sign-ins, and when the last invitation was sent, with Send invitation or Resend invitation, or, for a student whose account the program has still to confirm, a line saying the Administrators send the invitation once they have confirmed it. The button sends the program's own welcome invitation with a new link, which replaces the link in the earlier email. A student can be sent one invitation every fifteen minutes, and your institution twenty a day;
  • a table of Program, Internship duration, Cohort, Field of study, Tutor, WordPress.org, Contribution teams and Personal website, and then Mentor, which reads "No mentor yet" for a student with none on record. Mentor email is there only when the student has a mentor, and it is the one email address the card shows; a mentor known by name and not by address keeps the row, and the row reads "Not set";
  • Student Report Card, a section that is closed until you open it. It is the student's own report, read from the program's records when you open it, so it needs JavaScript, and you cannot change it. A student with no progress record yet has none, and the card says "This student has no progress record yet, so there is no Student Report Card to show.";
  • Correct this student's details, described below;
  • Download this student's details and course grades as a CSV file;
  • a last line saying how long ago the roster and the student's own details were read.

A student without an account has none of this: no correction form, no Finishing this placement and no download of their own. A change for such a student goes through your contact at the program.

A tutor reads the card and changes nothing: a tutor's card has no sign-in line, no correction form, no download and no Finishing this placement.

Correcting a student's details

Correct this student's details is a closed section under the Student Report Card. Open it and the form says "These five details are yours to correct." They are the Name on the Student Report Card, the Full name, the Start date, the End date and the Field of study. Everything else on the card is written by the program or by the student, and a change to any of it goes through your contact at the program.

Press Save changes. A date is written as YYYY-MM-DD, an end date has to be after the start date, a placement cannot run longer than a year, and the field of study has to be one of the program's own choices; Not set clears it. The program's records are written at once and the change is on your roster. The page says "Saved. The change is in the program records and on your roster." and adds a line to your institution's history, which the Administrators read. When a value is refused the form names what was refused and says whether the rest was saved, what you typed and was not saved stays in the form, and the section opens by itself so the sentence is not hidden. If the program's records hold two entries for one student, the dates and the field of study wait until an Administrator has merged them, and the name on the Student Report Card can still be corrected. A student with no progress record yet has no Student Report Card, and so has no correction section.

Finishing a placement

Under the student's card, Finishing this placement is a card of its own, where you record how a placement ended. The card offers Mark as dropped out. Mark as graduated is there only if the program switches it on; until it does, an Administrator records a graduation. Either one asks you to confirm first, because it sends the student a letter from the program straight away, and it cannot be undone from this page: an Administrator changes it back in the program's records. The card says why when it offers nothing, for example when the placement is already recorded as finished or the student is paused, and in that case your contact at the program is the one to ask.

Enrolling students

Enroll students is a view of its own, in a representative's menu once your agreement is accepted and the program has switched enrollment on for institutions, and Enroll students on the Overview opens it too. It opens with "Add students to the program, one at a time or from a list." Its address is the address of your Institution Dashboard with ?wpcpm_view=enroll added at the end: it takes you, or a representative at your institution you send it to, straight to the form and to the sample list in step 3, and it still does when they have to sign in first. A tutor who opens it is shown the Overview. Nothing is created until you have seen what the list was understood to say.

  1. Choose the Program the students are joining and the Start date, the term they begin; a date more than a year either side of today is refused as a typo. End date is optional, and has to be after the start date and at most a year after it. Tick the box that says these students have been notified that their name and email address are shared with the WordPress Foundation for the WordPress Credits Program; it has to be ticked.
  2. Add One student, with the Full name, the Email address, the Field of study and the Tutor, or send Or a list: A CSV file, picked with Choose a file, or the same text pasted into Or paste the same thing here. The Tutor box offers the tutors listed for your institution; while there are none it says "No tutors are listed for your institution yet. Add them under Tutors on Your institution, and they will appear here." A list needs a header row and then one student a line. Name and email are needed; field of study and tutor are read when they are there, other common spellings of the headings are read as well, and a column the import does not read is listed back to you and ignored. A list holds up to 300 students, and the file is read and never stored.
  3. Download a sample list, beside the file box, shows the format. The site makes it when you press: a CSV file with the four headings name, email, field_of_study and tutor and one example student. Keep the heading row and replace the example with your own students before you send it back: the example's address is one the import refuses on purpose, so a sample sent back unchanged creates nobody. The sample holds nothing about your institution or your students.
  4. Press Check the list. The page says how many rows can be created and gives every row a sentence: "Ready to create.", "Already on your roster", "Similar name on your roster" (that one is still created), "This student cannot be imported from here. Ask an Administrator.", "The same person as line" another line of the same list (neither is created), "This is the sample list's example student. Replace it with one of your students, or delete the row." (the example row of the sample list, which is never created, while the rest of your list is checked as usual), or what could not be read in the name or the address.
  5. Press Create these student records and confirm. The page repeats what is about to happen: how many records, on which program, from which start date. No email is sent when the records are created, and a student receives their login from the program when their account is created. Do not send these students to the registration form; it would create a second record. Throw this list away discards a list that has not been created. A long list is created in steps; the page says how many are done and how many are left, and Continue picks it up at once if you do not want to wait. When it ends it says how many were created, how many were blocked and how many the program's records refused.

Downloading lists

Download this cohort (CSV), beside the filters, gives a representative the whole cohort on the screen as a CSV file, with a column each for the roster group, the student, the program, the start and end dates, the cohort, the mentor, the WordPress.org profile, the team, the website, the field of study, the tutor and the hours. The group and the search narrow the page and leave the file whole. The Mentor column is blank for a student with none. A student's card has its own download, Download this student's details and course grades as a CSV file, which adds the grades of the student's course. A tutor is offered neither.

What your institution can and cannot see

The roster and the cards show your own students and no one else's. They never show a student's email address, and they never show what a student told the program in confidence about accessibility. Grades appear on a student's card and in that student's own download and nowhere else: they are not on the roster, in a count or in the semester report.

The semester report

At the end of a term the program drafts a report about the students your institution sent, and an Administrator reviews and approves it. Only then does your institution see it. You read it and download it; you do not write it.

Semester reports, in the menu, lists your institution's reports, one row for each semester. An approved report is tagged Approved, reads "Approved on" a date, and has View and Download PDF. A semester whose report is still being drafted says, for example, "Your semester report for January to June 2026 is being prepared by the program team." With none at all it says "No semester report has been published for your institution yet." Every account of your institution is emailed when a report is approved, and for thirty days the Overview names it under Good to know.

View opens the report in place of the list, with Download PDF above it, and Semester reports in the menu leads back to the list. Its headings are Program Overview, Participation, Contribution Teams, Student Projects and Blogs, Recognition and Events, Continuing Engagement, Student Feedback and Looking Ahead, less any an Administrator has taken out, with figures drawn from your students' records for that term and the words the Administrator wrote around them.

A student is named in it only if that student said you may, and a quote is shown only if the student released it, in the two permission questions at the end of their Finishing up feedback form. Those answers are read again each time the report is opened, so a student who changes their mind drops out of the report the next time anyone opens it, even one written weeks ago. When the students' answers cannot be read just now, the page says so and does not show the report.

Your details, your representatives and your agreement

Your institution, in the menu, opens with "What the program has on record about your institution, and who can see this page." It holds two cards, in this order: Your institution's details and Representatives and tutors. A tutor is shown only Representatives and tutors. Your Collaboration Agreement is a view of its own, Agreement. Your institution is in your menu once your agreement is accepted; before that, Agreement is where the work is, and you set your institution's name on the agreement document itself, as Before your agreement is accepted describes.

Your institution's details

The card lists eleven details under two small headings, then the tracks your institution offers. A detail the program holds nothing for reads Not given yet.

  • Contact and agreement: Contact person, Their role, Signs the agreement, Their title, Students study in and Page about WordPress Credits.
  • Name and address: Name, Website, City, Country and Contact's email.

Every representative of your institution reads the card and may correct its details; a tutor is not shown it. The two headings differ in one way. The contact and agreement details are yours to correct at once. The name and address details are asked for, and an Administrator decides. The program reaches your institution by the contact's email, files it by its country and shows its name on a public page, so a person at the program checks a change to any of them first.

Tracks offered lists the tracks your institution offers. The program sets them, not you: to change them, write to the program. When your institution offers two or more, its students are asked which track they want when they register.

Under each list is a closed section, named with what a save does, that opens the form for that list alone. The form asks the questions your institution answered when it applied, in the same words and with the same rules, and shows the value the program has: a box for a name, a web address or an email address, a list of ticks for the languages, and for the country one field that takes typing and narrows its list ("Type to find your country").

Correcting the contact and agreement details

Open Correct these (saved at once) under the first list, change what is wrong and press Save the details. The contact person is written to the program's records and the other details are kept on this site, straight away, the Administrators are emailed what changed and from what to what, and a line is added to your institution's history. The page says "Your institution's details are saved."

If a value is refused, the page says "Nothing was saved. Correct what is marked below and save again." and puts the reason under the box that has one; what you typed stays in the form. If the program's records cannot be written just now, it says "The program records could not be updated, so nothing was saved. Try again in a while." and nothing is saved here either, so the form and the records cannot disagree. If this site cannot keep the details that live on it, it says "The details could not be kept on the site, so nothing was saved. Try again in a while." A form sent with nothing changed says "Nothing was changed." and sends no email, and so does the same change sent again from another tab, or by a colleague, a moment after the first was saved. If a save of your institution's details is being made at that very moment, the page says "Someone else is saving your institution's details at this moment, so nothing was done. Try again in a moment." and what you typed stays in the form. A website or a page address with a space in it, or whose host has no dot, is refused the same way, under "Enter a web address such as example.com.".

Asking to correct the name and address

Open Ask to correct these (an Administrator checks first) under the second list, change what is wrong and press Send to an Administrator. Nothing is written yet. The page says "Sent: an Administrator checks the change, and you will see it here once it is decided." and the Administrators are emailed that a request is waiting. A refused value stays in the form with its reason, and the page says "Nothing was sent. Correct what is marked below and send it again." A form with nothing changed says "Nothing was changed." If your institution's details are being saved, or a colleague's request sent, at that very moment, the page says "Someone else is saving your institution's details at this moment, so nothing was done. Try again in a moment.", nothing is sent, and what you typed stays in the form.

An Administrator approves the request or declines it, as a whole and never a detail at a time. On approval the program's records are written with what you asked for, and the account that asked is emailed what changed. On a decline the Administrator writes a note for you, and the account that asked is emailed the note.

Your institution has one request at a time. While one waits, the second list offers no form, and a colleague who asks meanwhile, from another account or another browser tab, is told "One change is already waiting for an Administrator." and nothing is made.

While a request waits, and after it is decided

Under each row the request would change, the card says "Waiting for an Administrator:" with what was asked and the day it was asked, and Withdraw it. Any representative of your institution can press it, not only the account that asked; it takes the whole request back, says "The request is withdrawn." and tells the Administrators. If an Administrator decided the request a moment earlier, the page says so and nothing changes, and if a colleague, or another tab of yours, withdrew it first, the page says "Nothing was changed: that request had already been withdrawn."

Once the request is decided, every representative of your institution reads what became of it under the second list, until the next request is sent. After an approval the card says "Updated on" and the day. After a decline it says "An Administrator did not make the change you asked for:" and the note. After a withdrawal it says nothing.

Your representatives

Representatives and tutors lists the people who can sign in for your institution, with how many there are in its title. Each person has a row: the name, with a tag, the institution's contact, on the account whose email address is the one the program writes to, and under it the email address, whether they are a Representative or a Tutor, and how their access came about and since when ("Added by an Administrator", "Joined by invitation" and so on). When the program's records name a contact who has no account here yet, that person is listed too, with the sentence "Named in the program records, with no account on this site yet. An Administrator can add one so they can see this page.", and is not counted in the title, since they cannot sign in yet. When that address belongs to an account that was removed from your institution, the sentence is "Named in the program records. Their account is no longer among this institution's people. An Administrator can add them again." A tutor reads only "Named in the program records.", and so does everyone when that account now belongs to another institution. Everyone with an account can see your students. Representatives can remove anyone, themselves included. A tutor sees the students, their Student Report Cards and the semester reports, and changes nothing, so a tutor is shown no Remove and no Leave, no invitations waiting and no invitation form.

  • Remove takes a colleague's access away, and Leave on your own row takes yours. The page asks you to confirm first. The account is kept and nobody at the institution is emailed; when no one would be left, the Administrators are told. The program goes on writing to the contact's address until an Administrator changes it. To change who the program writes to, correct the Contact person with Correct these and ask to correct the Contact's email with Ask to correct these.
  • Invitations waiting lists the invitations not yet accepted, each with who sent it, when, and the day it stops working. Resend sends a new link, and the link in the earlier email stops working; Cancel invitation asks first, then stops the link at once.
  • Invite a colleague is a closed section. Open it, type the address in Email address, choose their Level and press Send invitation. They get one email with a link that is good for fourteen days. As the Level, Representative adds and changes students, invites colleagues and corrects the details; Tutor sees the students, their Student Report Cards and the semester reports, and changes nothing. Whoever accepts it sees the same students you do, and a representative can remove anybody, including you. Up to ten invitations can be waiting at a time, and each account can send five a day.
  • Tutors is a list of the people who tutor your students, with a name and an email address each. It is the list the Tutor box offers when you enroll a student. A representative or an Administrator can open Add a tutor, give the Name and the Email and press Add, and can Remove one. Adding a tutor sends no email and makes no account, and Remove asks first. Removing a tutor takes the name off the list and leaves the person's account, if they have one, and the students already assigned to them as they are. A tutor who accepts a Tutor invitation is added to the list. The same name with two addresses is two entries, and the box offers the name once. A tutor sees the list and cannot change it.

A person who follows an invitation sees a page that asks "Accept this invitation?" and nothing happens until they press Accept invitation. If they have no account yet one is made for them, and they get an email with a link to set a password. The invitation works for the address it was sent to. An Administrator can also add an account for a colleague; ask your contact at the program.

Your Collaboration Agreement

Once it is accepted, Agreement opens under the name Collaboration Agreement, with "The agreement between your institution and the program, and the signed copy on file." It is tagged Accepted, with the day it was accepted, and says how: "Signed and accepted through this site.", or that it was recorded from the program's own records or by an Administrator from the copy the program holds. Download the accepted agreement gives you the file when this site holds one; an agreement signed before this site existed is a copy the program holds itself, and there is no file to download. A tutor sees the Accepted tag, the day and how it was signed, with no download and no form.

Under it is the form to replace it, which begins "Replace it by uploading a newer signed copy. The agreement above stays in force until an Administrator accepts the new one." It is the same upload form as before your agreement was accepted, with Choose a file for the PDF. While a newer copy waits, the page says "A newer signed agreement is waiting for review. The agreement above stays in force until an Administrator accepts it.", with Download the copy waiting for review and Withdraw it.

If an Administrator revokes the agreement, everybody at your institution is emailed the reason. A representative's menu goes back to Overview and Agreement, with the reason on Agreement and a form to upload a new signed agreement: Before your agreement is accepted has the rest. A tutor cannot open the page until a new agreement is accepted.
